title: Introduce sample-and-hold KV-cache probe and scheduler-latency histograms with Grafana export
author: Maya Thompson
release_notes: Added a low-overhead 'sample-and-hold' KV-cache probe and per-scheduler latency histogram export. New Grafana push exporter for heatmap visualizations. Backwards-compatible instrumentation; no config changes required by default.
description:
Motivation:
Production workloads showed intermittent latency spikes that were not visible with existing coarse counters. The goal here is to add a low-overhead sampling probe for the KV cache hot-path that preserves temporal locality (sample-and-hold) and to surface scheduler queue/dispatch latencies as compact histograms that can be exported to our Grafana dashboards as heatmaps. This gives SREs and runtime engineers a fast feedback loop to correlate batching behavior, KV cache hits, and scheduling jitter without adding steady-state overhead.

What this PR does (high level):
- Implements a sample-and-hold KV-cache probe (runtime/kvcache/sample_hold_sampler.cc/.h) that samples keys at a tunable rate and holds a short-lived observation (ms granularity) to compute hit/miss heat and per-key latency summaries. The sampler is async-signal-safe and uses a small ringbuffer to avoid allocations on the hot path.
- Adds scheduler-latency histograms (runtime/scheduler/latency_hist.cc/.h) that bucket queue-to-dispatch and dispatch-to-complete times into exponential bins and maintain HDR-like summaries suitable for export.
- Introduces a lightweight Grafana push exporter (observability/grafana/heatmap_exporter.cc) that periodically flushes heatmap and histogram aggregates to the pushgateway endpoint used by our dashboarding pipeline. The exporter emits compressed protobuf payloads and supports tenant-scoped aggregation keys.
- Adds a microbenchmark and CI smoke test (tools/microbench/sample_hold_bench.py and tests/instrumentation/sample_hold_smoke_test.cc) to validate overheads and functional correctness.
- Documentation: docs/instrumentation/sample-and-hold.md with configuration knobs, expected resource usage, and dashboard panels.

Design notes and tradeoffs:
- Sampling strategy: the sample-and-hold approach chooses an incoming key with a tunable probability p, records the access latency and whether the request hit or missed the KV cache, and then 'holds' that key for a short epoch (default 50ms) to aggregate subsequent accesses. This reduces per-request overhead (only a small randomized branch) while preserving bursty behavior. We avoid full per-key maps to keep memory bounded on large cardinalities.
- Concurrency: the collector uses per-shard lock-free counters and a small fixed-size ring buffer for in-flight observations. We intentionally avoid heavy synchronization to keep tail latencies low. Review feedback asked for a lock-free period-writer; this implementation uses atomic CAS loops and a sequence counter to ensure readers see consistent snapshots.
- Export semantics: exporter batches aggregates and pushes to Pushgateway every 5s. Export is best-effort: if push fails we backoff with jitter. Data is tenant-scoped to maintain query efficiency in Grafana.

Benchmarks and numbers (on r5-gpu-small synthetic):
- End-to-end 99th P90 latency regression: +0.4ms (sample rate 0.01) vs baseline with no instrumentation.
- Microbench sample path overhead: ~45ns median extra per-request (probabilistic branch + fast path record).
- Memory increase: ~3.8MB per-instance (dominant contribution from ringbuffer and histogram buffers).

Review conversation (abridged):
- Arjun Patel: "Can we ensure the sample path is always inlined and has no allocations? Also worried about lock convoys in high concurrent shards."
  - Maya Thompson: "Sample path is marked inline and uses thread-local epoch counters; ringbuffer uses preallocated slices. I added a microbench proving no allocations on the hot path and updated readme with design notes."
- Lina Gómez: "Histogram bins look fine, but we'd prefer HDR-derived bins to match existing observability tooling."
  - Maya Thompson: "I switched to an exponential-bucket layout compatible with our profiler; we also expose a translation helper in observability/grafana for dashboard queries."
- Noah Reed: "Exporter needs throttling/backpressure for high-cardinality tenants."
  - Maya Thompson: "Added tenant-level cap and a per-tenant backpressure counter; when cap is hit, we sample aggregates at a coarser granularity."

Why this is safe to ship:
- Feature defaults to disabled for low-risk rollout (instrumentation enabled via runtime flag INSTRUMENT_SAMPLE_HOLD_KVCACHE).
- All heap allocations avoided on the fast path; microbench evidence included.
- Exporter is best-effort and will not block request processing.

Merge decision: squash-merged after addressing Lina's bucket feedback and adding the tenant cap. Change log entry and docs updated.

If you want to try locally:
- Build with: bazel build //runtime/... //observability/...
- Enable sampler: export REDWOOD_RUNTIME_FLAGS=INSTRUMENT_SAMPLE_HOLD_KVCACHE=1; start runtime; load sample_workload from tools/microbench.
